title: From Phenotype to Endotype in Neuro-EDS: A Framework for Mechanistic Investigation and Precision Care—How Can Neuro-EDS Be Biologically Characterized, Mechanistically Understood, Objectively Evaluated, and More Precisely Treated?
content: A subset of patients with hypermobile Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (hEDS), hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD), and related heritable connective tissue disorders (HCTDs) develop complex neurological manifestations. A companion position paper proposed Neuro-EDS as a recognizable neuro-predominant phenotype within this population, providing a foundation for standardized clinical characterization, patient stratification, and future mechanistic research. However, phenotypic characterization alone does not establish the biological mechanisms underlying disease expression.To address this gap, we introduce a phenotype-to-endotype framework for Neuro-EDS, reflecting a broader shift in medicine toward biologically informed classification of complex diseases. Central to this framework is the recognition that altered connective-tissue and extracellular-matrix (ECM) biology may provide a shared substrate through which distinct or interacting mechanisms contribute to seemingly disparate clinical manifestations. Organized around the principal clinical manifestations of Neuro-EDS, the framework integrates candidate biological mechanisms, potential modifiers of disease expression, and mechanism-linked verifiers—objective structural, physiological, functional, imaging, tissue-based, or molecular measures used to evaluate the presence and relevance of proposed mechanisms. This approach is intended to guide systematic mechanistic investigation and advance understanding of the biological basis of disease heterogeneity.Application of this framework may ultimately enable the identification and validation of biologically defined endotypes, facilitating earlier and more accurate diagnosis, improved patient stratification, and the development of precision therapies targeting underlying disease mechanisms. By providing a structured approach to objective mechanistic evaluation, the framework may also guide research priorities, improve comparability across studies, and support assessment of whether therapeutic interventions modify their intended biological targets.
